newsitem.title: USA: Six-figure fine urged for House Speaker Gingrich.
newsitem.headline: Six-figure fine urged for House Speaker Gingrich.

text.p: House Speaker Newt Gingrich would be hit with a six-figure fine as well as a reprimand for admitted ethics violations under a recommendation made by a House ethics subcommittee, Democratic sources said on Friday.

The House of Representatives ethics committee was to consider the recommendation at a public hearing later on Friday and to pass along its own decision to the full House, which was to vote on Gingrich's punishment on Tuesday.

A Republican leadership aide said the sum to be paid by Gingrich would be from $150,000 to $200,000. The aide said the money would reimburse the ethics committee for "costs incurred for filing unreliable and inaccurate information." The aide said Republicans consider that "not techically a fine."
Gingrich, a Georgia Republican, has acknowledged providing false information to the committee but has said that it was not intentional.

He has also acknowledged that he failed to seek legal advice about whether the use of charitable contribitions to help finance a college course he taught would violate laws prohibiting the use of such funds for partisan purposes.
